day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Rome Fiumicino Airport at 22:30. Take the Leonardo Express train (€14) to Roma Termini, then connect via metro or bus to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night slice of pizza al taglio near Termini station (€3–5) – many spots stay open late for arriving travelers

day_by_day.notes: Keep your first night simple. Buy a 48-hour or 72-hour Roma Pass (€28–€38) online in advance for metro rides and museum discounts. Exchange or withdraw euros at the airport ATM for the best rates. Validate your train ticket before boarding.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Ruins early (opens 9:00 AM). Arrive at 9:00 AM to beat the crowds and the heat. Walk through the Forum where Julius Caesar once stood, explore the Arch of Titus, and climb Palatine Hill for panoramic views. Combo ticket with Colosseum is ~€16 – book online to skip queues. Spend 2–3 hours here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Colosseum (included in combo ticket) for a self-guided tour of the iconic amphitheater. Afterward, stroll through the Circus Maximus area (free) and the Aventine Hill to find the famous Knights of Malta keyhole with a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome – completely free and magical.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the charming Trastevere neighborhood for the evening. Explore the cobblestone streets, peek into the Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere (free), and enjoy the lively local atmosphere as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Grab a cornetto (croissant) and cappuccino at a local bar near the hotel (€2–3) – stand at the counter like a local to save money
meals.lunch: Pick up a supplì (fried rice ball) and sandwich from a street food vendor near the Forum (€5–7 total)
meals.dinner: Trastevere has great budget trattorias – try Tonnarello or Da Enzo al 29 for cacio e pepe or amatriciana pasta (€10–14 per person). Alternatively, grab a wood-fired pizza for ~€8

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – you'll cover 6–8 km today. Bring a refillable water bottle; Rome has free drinking fountains (nasoni) throughout the city. The Colosseum area gets extremely hot in June – start early and carry sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel (opens 9:00 AM – book tickets online in advance for ~€17 to avoid the notorious 2-hour queues). Arrive at opening time and head straight to the Sistine Chapel before crowds build. Allow 3 hours to explore the Raphael Rooms, Gallery of Maps, and Michelangelo's breathtaking ceiling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exit into St. Peter's Basilica (free entry – separate from museum ticket). Climb to the top of St. Peter's dome for stunning city views (€8 with elevator, €6 on foot). Explore the basilica's interior, including Michelangelo's Pietà. Afterward, stroll along Via della Conciliazione toward Castel Sant'Angelo (exterior views are free).
day_by_day.evening: Walk to the Piazza Navona (free) to admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers as the evening light hits. Then explore the nearby Campo de' Fiori market square, lively with locals in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at a neighborhood bar near the hotel (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic or grab a panino from a nearby alimentari (deli) around the Vatican neighborhood – eat in Piazza del Risorgimento (€5–7)
meals.dinner: Near Campo de' Fiori – try a slice of Roman-style pizza at Forno Campo de' Fiori (€3–5 per slice) or a full meal at a nearby trattoria (€10–13)

day_by_day.notes: Dress code is strictly enforced at the Vatican – cover shoulders and knees (no shorts or sleeveless tops). A scarf or light wrap works perfectly. The Vatican Museums are closed on Sundays (except the last Sunday of the month when entry is free but extremely crowded). Wednesday is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Experience (MUST book in advance – mandatory timed entry, €15 + €2 booking fee, entry slots every 2 hours). Marvel at Bernini's extraordinary baroque sculptures including Apollo and Daphne, and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings. The gallery limits visitors to ensure an intimate, uncrowded experience – one of Rome's true hidden gems.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, spend the afternoon in the surrounding Villa Borghese gardens (free) – Rome's Central Park. Rent a rowboat on the lake (€5–6), explore the gardens on foot, or rent a bike. Walk down the Spanish Steps (free) nearby and toss a coin in the Trevi Fountain (free to view).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the upscale but walkable Prati neighborhood near the Vatican for window shopping, then head to a local enoteca (wine bar) for an aperitivo hour – many bars offer free snacks with a glass of house wine (€4–6).

meals.breakfast: Bar near the hotel – espresso and cornetto (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese gardens – pick up fresh bread, cheese, and fruit from a local alimentari or the Mercato Trionfale market (€6–8)
meals.dinner: Prati neighborhood has excellent budget trattorias – look for fixed-price lunch menus (often available at dinner too) for €10–12 including pasta, main, and water

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets sell out weeks in advance, especially in summer – book as soon as possible online at galleriaborghese.it. The gallery only allows 2-hour visits. Combine this with the gardens for a relaxed, art-filled day. The Spanish Steps area can be crowded – visit the Trevi Fountain early evening for better photos.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the lesser-known but stunning Capitoline Museums (€15 – the world's oldest public museums, housing the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue and incredible Roman sculptures). Enjoy views over the Forum from the terrace. Afterward, visit the nearby Mouth of Truth (Bocca della Verità) at Santa Maria in Cosmedin church – free, small donation appreciated.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a self-guided walking tour of Rome's beautiful piazzas – Piazza Venezia, Largo di Torre Argentina (ancient temple ruins with a cat sanctuary – free), and the Jewish Ghetto neighborhood. Browse the Portico d'Ottavia ruins and soak in 2,000 years of layered history.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Testaccio neighborhood – Rome's authentic food district. Visit the Testaccio Market (closes around 3 PM, so peek in if arriving early enough) and explore the neighborhood's street food scene in the evening. This is where Romans actually eat.

meals.breakfast: Try a maritozzo (cream-filled bun) at a local pasticceria – a Roman breakfast specialty (€2–3 with coffee)
meals.lunch: Testaccio Market or nearby street food – try supplì, porchetta sandwich, or artichokes alla romana (€5–8)
meals.dinner: Testaccio is budget heaven – Flavio al Velavevodetto or Da Remo for Roman-style thin-crust pizza (€7–10). Try coda alla vaccinara (oxtail stew) if feeling adventurous

day_by_day.notes: Friday evenings in Rome are lively – neighborhoods like Trastevere and Testaccio fill with locals. This is a great day to simply wander and get lost in Rome's authentic atmosphere. Many churches are free to enter and contain world-class art – San Luigi dei Francesi has three Caravaggio paintings (free).

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning day trip to Ostia Antica (€12 entry, ~30 min by train from Roma Ostiense station, €1.50 train ticket). This remarkably preserved ancient Roman port city rivals Pompeii but is far less crowded and cheaper. Explore the ancient baths, amphitheater, taverns, and mosaic floors – allow 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Rome by early afternoon. Visit the Pantheon (€5 entry since 2023 – one of the best-preserved ancient buildings in the world). Spend time in the Piazza della Rotonda and surrounding streets. Pop into the nearby Sant'Ignazio church (free) with its stunning trompe-l'œil ceiling.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your Saturday evening at the lively Piazza Navona street scene, then walk along the scenic Lungotevere riverside promenade as the sun sets over the Tiber. End the evening with a gelato crawl – compare a few gelaterias (look for 'artigianale' signs for authentic, natural gelato at €2–3 per scoop).

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast from a nearby bar to eat on the train to Ostia (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Bring a packed lunch to Ostia Antica or eat at the small café inside the site (€5–8). Alternatively, eat upon return to Rome near the Pantheon
meals.dinner: Near Piazza Navona – avoid the tourist traps directly on the piazza. Walk one block away for authentic Roman trattorias (€12–15). Try cacio e pepe – Rome's signature pasta dish

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the busiest day at major sites – Ostia Antica is a brilliant way to escape the crowds while still experiencing remarkable ancient history. If you prefer to stay in Rome, the MAXXI (National Museum of 21st Century Arts) offers a modern art contrast for €12. Gelato tip: avoid places with piled-up, brightly colored gelato – authentic gelato is stored in covered metal containers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the famous Porta Portese flea market in Trastevere (every Sunday, 7:00 AM – 2:00 PM, free entry). Browse hundreds of stalls selling vintage clothes, antiques, books, and curiosities – a wonderful slice of Roman life. Practice your bargaining and pick up unique souvenirs without tourist markup.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your last afternoon revisiting your favorite spots or exploring any missed gems. Consider the free last Sunday of the month at state museums (Vatican Museums would be free if this falls on the last Sunday of June 2027 – check in advance). Alternatively, visit the Galleria Doria Pamphilj (€12) – a stunning private palazzo with Velázquez and Caravaggio works, rarely crowded.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Trastevere – splurge slightly on your last night with a sit-down meal at a neighborhood trattoria. Enjoy a final glass of local wine, tiramisu, and soak in the magic of Rome's most romantic neighborhood before heading back to the hotel to pack.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the market or a nearby bar (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Trastevere – a slice of pizza bianca with mortadella from a local forno (bakery), €4–6
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a Trastevere trattoria – budget €15–20 per person for a proper Roman meal with wine. Try tiramisu or panna cotta for dessert (€4–5)

day_by_day.notes: Pack the night before if your departure is early. Keep metro/bus tickets for the return journey to the airport. The Leonardo Express to Fiumicino runs every 30 minutes and takes 32 minutes (€14). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight. Rome tip: always ask for 'acqua del rubinetto' (tap water) at restaurants to avoid paying €3–4 for bottled water.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30. No morning or afternoon activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Rome Fiumicino Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take a pre-booked airport taxi or Leonardo Express train to Termini, then transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport before departure.
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite near the hotel — look for a 24-hour bar or pizzeria al taglio (pizza by the slice) for a casual €5–10 snack before bed.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 completely light. Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid long taxi queues late at night. Exchange some euros at the airport or withdraw from an ATM upon arrival. Set out your comfortable walking shoes for the busy days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Slow start — enjoy a leisurely Italian breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café. After settling in, take a gentle orientation stroll around your neighborhood to get your bearings. Visit a local market or piazza to soak in the Roman morning atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Ruins. Walk through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire, exploring the Forum where Julius Caesar once stood, the Arch of Titus, and the sweeping views from Palatine Hill. Book tickets online in advance to skip the queues. Budget approx. €16–18 per person (includes Colosseum access).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll over to the nearby Trastevere neighborhood for the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk. Wander cobblestone streets sampling supplì (fried rice balls), Roman-style artichokes, local wines, and other street bites with a knowledgeable local guide. A wonderful introduction to Roman food culture.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel — cornetto (Italian croissant) and cappuccino, approx. €3–5.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near the Roman Forum area — try Pizzarium or a local trattoria for cacio e pepe or a simple pasta dish, approx. €12–18.
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk tastings. Supplement with a glass of house wine at a Trastevere enoteca if still hungry, approx. €5–10 extra.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable, closed-toe shoes for the uneven cobblestones and ruins. Bring sunscreen and a water bottle — June in Rome can be warm. The Trastevere walk typically starts around 18:30–19:00; confirm exact time when booking.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel — book a timed entry slot well in advance (opens at 09:00). Spend the morning exploring one of the world's greatest art collections: the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and the breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling by Michelangelo. Budget 3–4 hours minimum. Entry approx. €20–25 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, visit St. Peter's Basilica (free entry) and climb the dome for panoramic city views (approx. €6–8). Spend the rest of the afternoon wandering the Prati neighborhood around the Vatican — a charming, less-touristy area with great shops and cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the Tiber and explore the Castel Sant'Angelo area at dusk — beautifully lit and photogenic. Then head to a mid-range restaurant in the Prati or Campo de' Fiori area for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near the Vatican — grab a quick cornetto and espresso before the museum opens.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Prati neighborhood — try Pizzarium Bonci for world-famous pizza al taglio, approx. €10–15.
meals.dinner: Trattoria in Prati or Campo de' Fiori area — order classic Roman dishes like carbonara, coda alla vaccinara, or saltimbocca. Budget approx. €25–35 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: The Vatican is extremely crowded in June. Arrive at your timed slot promptly. Shoulders and knees must be covered to enter St. Peter's Basilica — carry a scarf or light layer. Consider a guided Vatican tour for deeper context (approx. €35–50 including entry).

day_by_day.morning: Pasta & Gelato Making Class — join a hands-on cooking class in a traditional Roman kitchen. A local chef teaches you to make fresh pasta from scratch and craft authentic gelato. Classes typically run 3–4 hours and include tasting everything you make. Book in advance; approx. €65–90 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the class, walk off your delicious lunch with a visit to the Pantheon (book timed entry, approx. €5) and the surrounding area. Explore Piazza Navona, admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers, and browse the artisan shops nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely evening around Piazza Navona and the historic center. Stop for an Aperol Spritz or Negroni at a rooftop bar for golden-hour views, then take a relaxed evening passeggiata (stroll) through the neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel — cappuccino and pastry, approx. €4–6.
meals.lunch: Included in the Pasta & Gelato Making Class — you eat what you cook!
meals.dinner: Light dinner after the big cooking class lunch — visit an enoteca (wine bar) near Piazza Navona for a charcuterie board, bruschette, and a glass of local Lazio wine. Budget approx. €20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class is a highlight of the trip — confirm your booking at least a week in advance as spots fill quickly. Wear comfortable clothes you don't mind getting a little floury. The Pantheon now requires advance ticket booking online.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Experience — visit this intimate gem housing Bernini's stunning baroque sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings. Entry is strictly timed and limited to 2-hour slots; reservations are mandatory. Book weeks ahead. Entry approx. €15–20 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, rent a rowboat on the scenic lake inside Villa Borghese park (approx. €5–10) or simply stroll through the beautiful gardens. From the Pincio Terrace, enjoy one of Rome's finest panoramic views over the city rooftops. Then head down to the Spanish Steps and Via Condotti for window shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Trevi Fountain area at dusk (far less crowded than midday). Toss your coin, make your wish, and enjoy the magical illuminated fountain. Dine nearby in the Trevi or Quirinale district.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel or near Villa Borghese — cornetto and espresso, approx. €3–5.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese park — pick up supplies from a nearby deli or alimentari: fresh bread, local cheese, cured meats, and fruit. Budget approx. €10–15.
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant near the Trevi Fountain — try cacio e pepe or amatriciana followed by tiramisu. Budget approx. €28–40 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets are notoriously difficult to get last-minute — book as early as possible, ideally the moment you confirm your trip. Villa Borghese park is perfect for a midday rest in the shade. The Trevi Fountain is most magical and less crowded after 20:00.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's authentic food district. Visit the Testaccio Market (open until 14:00) for fresh produce, local cheeses, street food stalls, and a glimpse of everyday Roman life. Try supplì, porchetta sandwiches, and fresh fruit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the non-Catholic Cemetery (Cimitero Acattolico) — a beautifully serene and artistic hidden gem where Keats and Shelley are buried. Then explore the Aventine Hill: visit the Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) for stunning city views and peek through the famous Knights of Malta keyhole for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Trastevere for a final relaxed evening in one of Rome's most atmospheric neighborhoods. Enjoy an aperitivo hour, then settle into a candlelit restaurant for your last big dinner in the city.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Testaccio Market — fresh pastries and espresso from a market bar, approx. €4–6.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Testaccio Market food stalls — porchetta sandwich, suppli, and local snacks, approx. €10–15.
meals.dinner: Trastevere trattoria dinner — try cacio e pepe, grilled lamb chops (abbacchio), and finish with a classic Roman dessert. Budget approx. €30–40 per person including house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday mornings at Testaccio Market are lively and fun — go early (before 11:00) for the best experience before the crowds arrive. The Knights of Malta keyhole view is free and takes only a moment but is genuinely magical. Book your Trastevere dinner restaurant in advance on Saturday evenings as they fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Slow, savoring final morning in Rome. Visit one of Rome's beautiful Sunday markets — Porta Portese flea market in Trastevere (runs until 14:00) is Rome's largest and most famous, perfect for browsing vintage finds, art prints, and unique souvenirs. Alternatively, revisit a favorite piazza or art spot you want to see one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gelato tour — spend the afternoon on a self-guided gelato crawl, visiting 2–3 of Rome's best artisan gelaterias (try Giolitti, Fatamorgana, or Gelateria dei Gracchi). Pack your bags back at the hotel, do a final check of your room, and check out.
day_by_day.evening: Depending on your departure time, enjoy a final aperitivo in a rooftop bar overlooking the city. Transfer to the airport or train station for your onward journey, carrying wonderful Roman memories with you.

meals.breakfast: Final Roman café breakfast — sit down (rather than standing at the bar) to savor the moment. Cappuccino and a warm cornetto, approx. €5–8.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Porta Portese or back in Trastevere — a simple pizza margherita or a panino from a local bar, approx. €10–15.
meals.dinner: Airport dinner or a farewell meal near the hotel before departure — keep it simple and budget-friendly, approx. €15–25.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Fiumicino. Store luggage at the hotel if you have a late flight (most hotels offer this service). Pick up any last-minute food souvenirs — pasta, olive oil, wine, or biscotti — at a Eataly store or a local alimentari before heading to the airport.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery strictly limits visitors — book 2–3 months in advance for preferred time slots. Dress code applies at fine dining restaurants; smart-casual at minimum, jacket recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive skip-the-line private tour of the Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel. A personal art historian guide leads you through the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and finally into the awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel — ideally during a special early-morning access session before general public entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the grandeur of St. Peter's Basilica and climb to the top of the dome for sweeping panoramic views of Rome. Afterward, cross the Tiber to the charming Trastevere neighborhood for a relaxed afternoon exploring its golden-hued medieval streets and artisan boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Join the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — a curated culinary stroll through cobblestone alleys sampling supplì, Roman-style artichokes (carciofi alla giudia), aged Pecorino Romano, and pairing local wines at hidden enotecas beloved by Romans.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the Vatican tour — light yet energizing: Greek yogurt with honey, a warm brioche, and espresso
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ristorante Il Sorpasso near the Vatican — Roman classics like carbonara and abbacchio (roast lamb) in a sophisticated bistro setting
meals.dinner: The Trastevere food walk serves as your progressive dinner — conclude with dessert at a historic gelateria, ordering pistachio and ricotta e fiele flavors

day_by_day.notes: Vatican early-morning access (before 8:00 AM) is available through select tour operators — highly recommended to avoid crowds. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the evening food walk on cobblestones. Modest dress required for the Vatican (covered shoulders and knees).

day_by_day.morning: Immersive Pasta & Gelato Making Class in a traditional Roman kitchen. A celebrated local chef guides you through hand-rolling fresh cacio e pepe pasta, crafting amatriciana from scratch, and churning artisanal gelato using seasonal Roman ingredients. A deeply personal and delicious experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-class, visit the Campo de' Fiori market (winding down by early afternoon) for gourmet Italian pantry finds — truffle oils, aged balsamic, and artisan pasta to bring home. Then explore the nearby Jewish Ghetto, one of Rome's oldest and most atmospheric neighborhoods, with a private historian.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on a rooftop bar overlooking the Roman skyline — try the terrace at Hotel Raphael or Terrazza Borromini for Negronis and cicchetti. Follow with dinner at a prestigious restaurant in the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — eggs Benedict Roman-style with prosciutto crudo, freshly squeezed juice, and a cappuccino
meals.lunch: The cooking class itself serves as lunch — you dine on everything you prepare, paired with regional Italian wines selected by the chef
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Pierluigi in the historic center — celebrated for its seafood, innovative Roman dishes, and beautiful outdoor terrace

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes book out weeks in advance — confirm through the resort concierge upon arrival. The Jewish Ghetto tour pairs beautifully with the afternoon Campo de' Fiori visit as both are within walking distance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided exploration of the Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Ruins — walk where Julius Caesar addressed the Senate, explore the Arch of Titus, and ascend Palatine Hill for sweeping views over the ancient city. A knowledgeable archaeologist-guide brings 2,000 years of history vividly to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Colosseum with your guide (combined ticket covers Forum and Palatine Hill). Opt for exclusive underground and arena floor access for an unparalleled perspective. Afterward, decompress with a spa treatment back at the resort — a deep-tissue massage or Roman thermal ritual.
day_by_day.evening: Elegant dinner at Aroma Restaurant — Rome's only Michelin-starred restaurant with a direct view of the Colosseum, illuminated magnificently at night. An unmissable, once-in-a-lifetime dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Substantial resort breakfast to fuel a full day of walking — smoked salmon eggs, fresh fruit, pastries, and cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic prepared by the resort — charcuterie, artisan bread, local olives, and chilled rosé enjoyed on Palatine Hill with ancient Rome as your backdrop
meals.dinner: Aroma Restaurant tasting menu — innovative takes on Roman cuisine paired with an exceptional Italian wine list, with the Colosseum glowing outside your window

day_by_day.notes: Underground Colosseum access requires advance booking — arrange through a premium tour operator. The resort concierge should secure Aroma Restaurant reservations well in advance as tables are extremely limited. Comfortable but stylish footwear essential for ancient ruins.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private tour of the Capitoline Museums — the world's oldest public museums, housing Marcus Aurelius's original bronze equestrian statue, Caravaggio masterpieces, and the She-Wolf of Rome. Enjoy VIP access before general opening with a dedicated curator guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon on the Spanish Steps and Via Condotti — Rome's most prestigious shopping street. Browse Valentino, Bulgari, Gucci, and Fendi flagship stores. Stop into Antico Caffè Greco, Rome's oldest café (est. 1760), for a ceremonial espresso at the marble bar.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-eve celebration dinner at La Pergola — Rome's only three-Michelin-starred restaurant, perched atop the Rome Cavalieri hotel with panoramic city views. Chef Heinz Beck's extraordinary Mediterranean haute cuisine with an 800-label wine cellar. The pinnacle of Roman fine dining.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — indulge fully with a à la carte spread: eggs any style, pastries, fresh fruit, champagne if desired
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nino Ristorante near the Spanish Steps — a beloved Florentine-Roman institution frequented by artists and diplomats since 1934
meals.dinner: La Pergola tasting menu (8–10 courses) — a landmark culinary journey with full sommelier wine pairing. Reserve months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: La Pergola requires formal dress (jacket and tie for gentlemen, elegant attire for ladies) and reservations should be made 2–3 months ahead. This is the crown jewel dining experience of the trip — plan the entire day around an 8:00 PM reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome — a slow, savored breakfast at the resort. Take one last walk along the nearest piazza or waterfront to absorb the atmosphere. Visit a nearby artisan shop for last-minute luxury gifts — handmade leather goods, Murano glass, or a bottle of aged Brunello di Montalcino.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on flight time, enjoy a farewell espresso and pastry at a neighborhood bar. Private luxury transfer to Rome Fiumicino Airport arranged by the concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Rome — carrying extraordinary memories of art, ancient history, and world-class cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final resort breakfast — order your favorites from the week, savoring every last bite of Roman pastry and perfectly pulled espresso
meals.lunch: If time permits before departure, a final light lunch at a trattoria near the resort — simple cacio e pepe or a Roman-style pizza bianca as a delicious farewell
meals.dinner: In-flight or at the airport — the resort concierge can arrange a gourmet departure hamper with Italian cheeses, cured meats, wine, and sweets for the journey home

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security at Fiumicino. Request a late checkout from the resort if your flight departs in the evening. Ask the concierge to arrange luggage storage if needed for a final afternoon in the city.

query: Rome art and food trip, $2500, 7 days, June 2026 from Chicago
